title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 92–94). M is a set of objects ('multiplicités'), apparently strata or pieces of a tame space. It carries order-type relations ≤, ≪, and a disjointness relation ∥. Each X ∈ M has an 'open part' X°. The supports Σ_M are the sets closed for the biorthogonal (polar) closure with respect to ∥: Supp(E) = {Y : Y ∥ Z for every Z ∥ E}. So Σ_M is a complete lattice with an order-reversing involutive complementation C_M(S) = S^⊥, the 'anti-involution canonique' on the page. F is a figure (a stratified object), and F̃ = Φ ⊂ M is its set of mutually compatible pieces. For A ⊂ F̃, p. 92 defines S_A = Supp(∪_{X∈A} X°) = Sup_{Σ_M} Supp(X°). This gives a monotone map P(F̃) → Σ_M that commutes with unions by associativity of Sup.

The page states the theorem Grothendieck wants to prove:
(a) A ↦ S_A is injective; more precisely it is an order-isomorphism of P(F̃) onto an ordered subset of Σ_M.
(b) It commutes with arbitrary Sup (including transfinite ones) and arbitrary Inf.
(c) For B ⊂ A ⊂ F̃, S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ C_M(S_B), so set difference goes to relative orthocomplement.
(d) If A is closed in F̃, i.e. A = C̃ for C closed in F, then S_A is the support of the subfigure G = C, i.e. Supp_M̂(A).

The NB says S_A makes sense for any subset A ⊂ M made of mutually compatible objects, not only for the pieces of a given figure. Hence all the formulas can be restated as operations on such subsets of M (continued on p. 94).

In modern terms: a family of mutually compatible (pairwise disjoint-interior) pieces generates a complete Boolean subalgebra, isomorphic to a power set, inside the complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets of an orthogonality space. This is the axiomatic core of showing that a stratified figure is recovered from its supports. Page 94 begins the proof: injectivity is reduced to Lemma 8, X° ⊂ S_B ⇒ X ∈ B.
errors: (c), and the Inf part of (b), do not follow from the general properties of the closure Supp. In a general ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets, S_A = S_{A∖B} ∨ S_B with S_{A∖B} ⊥ S_B does not force S_A ∧ S_B^⊥ = S_{A∖B}; that needs orthomodularity or distributivity on the sublattice in question. So these clauses must rest on the specific compatibility axioms (Lemma 1, A1, Lemma 8). On this page they are only stated as a goal ('J'aimerais prouver'), not proved.
Minor: in (a), 'sous-ensemble ordonné' should really be a sub-lattice (Boolean) given (b) and (c); the statement is slightly under-formulated.

ideas.what: Supports as biorthogonally closed sets of a disjointness relation, with a canonical complementation C_M
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / Galois-closed sets forming a complete ortholattice

ideas.what: Mutually compatible pieces of a figure generate a Boolean (power-set) subalgebra of the support lattice, preserving all Sup/Inf and relative complements
ideas.modern_name: Compatible elements generate a Boolean subalgebra (Foulis–Holland type result); recovery of a stratification from its lattice of supports
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs is unpublished; the tame-topology programme is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic 'analysis situs' builds a complete ortholattice of supports from a disjointness relation and needs compatible families to behave Booleanly. This is exactly the structure studied in quantum logic and orthogonality spaces, a link not made in the literature on tame topology or stratified spaces.
missed.quote: où C_M est l'anti-involution canonique de l'ens. des supports
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Orthomodular-lattice tools could supply or simplify the proofs of (b) and (c), and could clarify which axioms on strata make the support lattice orthomodular. That matters for lattice-theoretic or pointless approaches to o-minimal or stratified geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent but programmatic intermediate theorem inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft. The ortholattice flavour is mildly interesting, but the content is foundational bookkeeping and is not proved on this page.
transcription_corrections: (b): 'Cette application est commutative aux Sup quelconques (transfinis généralisés) et aux Inf quelconques'. 'quelc.' is a marginal insertion after 'Sup'.
(d): roughly 'Si A est une partie fermée de F̃ (donc de la forme C̃, où C est fermé dans F) ... on a S_A = Supp G ≝ Supp_M̂(A)'.
NB: roughly 'En fait, S_A est défini dès qu'on se donne, au lieu de F où F̃ = Φ ⊂ M, ... une partie A ⊂ M formée d'un ensemble de multiplicités mutuellement compatibles.'
Last line is likely 'Donc toutes ces formules précédentes peuvent [être]', continuing into 'formulées ainsi' on p. 94.
